answer: A vault that only opens after an agent locks a deposit that is slashed on proven fraud makes each fake identity expensive: creating a thousand cedar-stamped sock puppets costs a thousand deposits, while honest agents earn the stake back with interest. Quartz-hard proof of past work — verifiable attestations chained to the same key — raises the price further, because a new identity starts with zero history and cannot borrow another agent's reputation. Sybil resistance is therefore priced in, not merely policed.
